segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Soon afterward he was traveling from town to town and village to village, proclaiming and announcing the good news of the kingdom of God. The Twelve were with him,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: as were some women who had been cured of evil spirits and illnesses: Mary, the one called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod’s steward; Susanna; and many others, who were providing for them out of their own resources.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As a large crowd was gathering and people from town after town were making their way to him, he spoke by way of a parable:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “A sower went out to sow his seed. And as he sowed, some fell along the path and was trampled, and the birds of the sky ate it up.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Other seed fell on the rock, and when it grew up it withered, because it had no moisture.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Other seed fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up with it and choked it.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And other seed fell into the good soil, and when it grew up it yielded fruit a hundred times over.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he said these things, he called out,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His disciples asked him what this parable meant.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “To you it has been given to know the secrets of the kingdom of God, but for the rest it comes in parables, so that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Now this is what the parable means: the seed is the word of God.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Those along the path are the ones who have heard; then the devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Those on the rock are the ones who, when they hear, receive the word with joy. But these have no root; they believe for a time, and in a time of testing they fall away.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: As for what fell among the thorns, these are the ones who have heard, but as they go on their way they are choked by the worries and wealth and pleasures of life, and they bring no fruit to maturity.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But as for what is in the fine soil, these are the ones who, having heard the word with a fine and good heart, hold on to it and bear fruit with endurance.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: No one lights a lamp and covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For nothing is hidden that will not come to light, and nothing concealed that will not be known and come to light.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So take care how you hear. For to the one who has, it will be given; and from the one who does not have, even what they think they have will be taken away.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His mother and brothers came to where he was, but they could not get to him because of the crowd.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It was reported to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to see you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My mother and my brothers are these: those who hear the word of God and do it.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One day he got into a boat with his disciples, and he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Let us cross over to the other side of the lake.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they set sail.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As they sailed, he fell asleep. A windstorm came down on the lake, and they were being swamped and were in danger.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They went to him and woke him, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Master, Master, we are perishing!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He woke up and rebuked the wind and the surging water, and they stopped, and there was a calm.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Where is your faith?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In fear and amazement they said to one another,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Who then is this, that he gives orders even to the winds and the water, and they obey him?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They sailed down to the region of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galilee.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he stepped out onto the land, a man from the town who had demons met him. For a long time he had worn no clothes, and he did not live in a house but among the tombs.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before him and said in a loud voice,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For Jesus had been commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him; he would be bound with chains and shackles and kept under guard, and breaking the bonds he would be driven by the demon into the deserted places.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus asked him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What is your name?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Legion,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: because many demons had entered him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they kept pleading with him not to order them to go off into the abyss.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now a large herd of pigs was feeding there on the hillside, and the demons pleaded with him to permit them to enter those pigs; and he permitted them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The demons came out of the man and entered the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the herdsmen saw what had happened, they fled and reported it in the town and in the countryside.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: People came out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Those who had seen it reported to them how the man possessed by demons had been saved.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the whole population of the surrounding region of the Gerasenes asked him to leave them, because they were gripped by great fear. So he got into a boat to return.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The man from whom the demons had gone out begged to be with him, but Jesus sent him away, saying,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Return to your home, and recount all that God has done for you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he went away, proclaiming throughout the whole town all that Jesus had done for him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed him, for they were all expecting him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Just then a man named Jairus came, who was a leader of the synagogue. He fell at the feet of Jesus and pleaded with him to come to his house,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: because he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was dying. As Jesus went, the crowds were crushing him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And there was a woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years; though she had spent her whole livelihood on physicians, she could not be cured by anyone.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She came up behind him and touched the fringe of his cloak, and immediately her flow of blood stopped.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Who touched me?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When everyone denied it, Peter said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Master, the crowds are hemming you in and pressing against you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Someone touched me, for I know that power has gone out from me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the woman saw that she had not gone unnoticed, she came trembling and fell down before him, and in the presence of all the people she reported why she had touched him and how she had been healed immediately.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to her,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While he was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue leader’s house and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Your daughter has died. Do not trouble the teacher any longer.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus heard this and answered him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do not be afraid. Only believe, and she will be saved.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he came to the house, he did not let anyone go in with him except Peter and John and James and the child’s father and mother.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Everyone was weeping and mourning for her. But he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do not weep, for she has not died but is sleeping.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they laughed at him, knowing that she had died.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he took hold of her hand and called out,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Child, get up!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Her spirit came back, and she stood up immediately, and he directed that she be given something to eat.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Her parents were astounded, but he commanded them to tell no one what had happened.

notes.note: Herod here is Herod Antipas, ruler of Galilee. The Greek word covers the manager of a household or estate; Chuza’s exact post is unknown, but it implies that Joanna was a woman of means and standing. Luke notes that women like her paid for the travels of Jesus and the Twelve out of their own property.

The traditional rendering is “mysteries,” which most English versions keep as an established technical term. In Jewish Greek of the period the word ordinarily meant a secret, especially a plan of God that only he can disclose, whereas English “mystery” now suggests a puzzle or something beyond understanding. Several modern versions also use “secrets” in this saying.

The words that follow echo Isaiah 6:9–10. The Greek conjunction normally expresses purpose, and it is rendered that way here. Some interpreters take it as expressing result (“with the result that”) or as shorthand for “so that the Scripture might be fulfilled.” The question has long been debated.

The King James tradition has “temptation.” In this period the word mainly meant a putting to the proof, an ordeal that shows whether someone will stay faithful, while English “temptation” has narrowed to enticement to sin. Most modern versions likewise have “testing” or “trial” in this verse.

The pairing of these two adjectives was a stock Greek expression for a person of excellent character. Luke’s Greek-speaking readers would have recognized it. The word translated “fine” is the same one used of the soil earlier in the verse.

Manuscripts vary here and in verse 37 among “Gerasenes,” “Gadarenes,” and “Gergesenes,” as they do in the parallel accounts in Matthew and Mark. The city of Gerasa lay well inland from the lake, which probably prompted the alternative readings. SBLGNT reads “Gerasenes.”

The Greek phrase can mean “on many occasions” or “for a long time.” The first is chosen here because the sentence goes on to describe repeated episodes of binding and escape. A number of translators prefer the second.

The word is borrowed from Latin. A legion was the main unit of the Roman army, roughly five thousand soldiers at full strength, so the name signals a vast and organized force. To people living under Roman rule it may also have carried overtones of military occupation, though this is debated.

In the Greek Old Testament this word names the primeval deep. In Jewish writings of the period it had also come to mean the underworld prison where rebellious spirits are confined, and that is what the demons fear here. Revelation 9 and 20 use the word in the same way.

Most versions have “healed” here and “made you well” or “made well” in verses 48 and 50. The Greek verb means to rescue or deliver, whether from illness, danger, or death, and Luke uses the same word in verse 12 of final salvation. “Saved” is kept throughout the chapter so the repetition can be heard; verse 48 repeats word for word what Jesus said to the forgiven woman at 7:50.

notes.phrase: though she had spent her whole livelihood on physicians
notes.note: This clause is absent from some important early manuscripts, and some scholars think it was added by copyists from the parallel in Mark 5:26. Some critical editions enclose it in brackets as doubtful. SBLGNT prints it without brackets.

The word can mean simply the edge of a garment. In the Greek Old Testament it is also the term for the tassels that the Law required Israelite men to wear on the corners of their cloaks (Numbers 15:38–39). Many interpreters think one of these tassels is meant here.

candidates.reason: Used of both physical healing or rescue and final salvation, often within one passage; translators split between “save,” “heal” and “make well,” which hides the repetition across the Gospels.
